questions.question: Who first excavated Harappa in 1921?
questions.explanation:
Daya Ram Sahni is correct: he excavated Harappa in 1921, the first site of this civilisation to be discovered.
James Prinsep is incorrect: he deciphered the Brahmi script of Ashokan inscriptions in 1837.
Max Muller is incorrect: he was a scholar of Sanskrit and the Vedas.
William Jones is incorrect: he founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal in 1784.
So the answer is Daya Ram Sahni.

questions.question: On the banks of which river is Mohenjodaro located?
questions.explanation:
Indus is correct: Mohenjodaro lies on the Indus in Sindh (Pakistan).
Ganga, Godavari and Kaveri are incorrect: these rivers flow far to the east and south, away from the main Harappan region.
So the answer is Indus.

questions.question: The Harappan civilisation belongs to which age?
questions.explanation:
Bronze Age is correct: the Harappans used copper and bronze tools.
Iron Age is incorrect: the Harappans did not know iron.
Old Stone Age is incorrect: that was the age of hunter-gatherers, long before cities.
Modern Age is incorrect: the Harappan cities flourished more than 4,000 years ago.
So the answer is Bronze Age.

questions.question: The Great Bath was found at which site?
questions.explanation:
Mohenjodaro is correct: the Great Bath is a large brick tank in the citadel of Mohenjodaro.
Pataliputra is incorrect: it was the Mauryan capital.
Hampi is incorrect: it was the capital of the Vijayanagara empire.
Taxila is incorrect: it is known for its ancient university and Gandhara remains.
So the answer is Mohenjodaro.

questions.question: Which metal was NOT known to the Harappans?
questions.explanation:
Iron is correct: no iron has been found in Harappan cities; iron came into use in India much later.
Copper is incorrect: copper was widely used for tools and vessels.
Gold is incorrect: gold was used for ornaments.
Bronze is incorrect: bronze (copper mixed with tin) was used, for example in the dancing girl figurine.
So the answer is Iron.

questions.question: Lothal, a Harappan site famous for its dockyard, is located in which present-day state?
questions.explanation:
Gujarat is correct: Lothal lies near the Gulf of Khambhat in Gujarat.
Bihar, Kerala and Assam are incorrect: no major Harappan city lies in these states.
So the answer is Gujarat.

questions.question: What is the present status of the Harappan script?
options: It has not yet been deciphered
It has been read as Sanskrit
It has been read as Tamil
It is the same as the Devanagari script
questions.explanation:
It has not yet been deciphered is correct: scholars still cannot read the Harappan script.
It has been read as Sanskrit and It has been read as Tamil are incorrect: such claims are not accepted because the script remains undeciphered.
It is the same as the Devanagari script is incorrect: Devanagari developed thousands of years later from Brahmi.
So the answer is that it has not yet been deciphered.

questions.question: Which famous bronze figurine was found at Mohenjodaro?
questions.explanation:
Dancing Girl is correct: this small bronze figurine was found at Mohenjodaro.
Sarnath Lion Capital is incorrect: it is a Mauryan stone pillar capital of Ashoka.
Nataraja is incorrect: the famous bronze Natarajas were made under the Cholas.
Gommateshwara is incorrect: it is a huge stone statue at Shravanabelagola in Karnataka.
So the answer is Dancing Girl.

questions.question: Harappan cities are well known for which feature?
questions.explanation:
Covered drains along the streets is correct: Harappan cities had a planned drainage system with covered drains.
Large Buddhist stupas is incorrect: Buddhism arose over a thousand years later.
Iron-roofed palaces is incorrect: the Harappans did not know iron.
Temples with tall towers is incorrect: no temples have been identified in Harappan cities.
So the answer is covered drains along the streets.

questions.question: Which animal appears most often on Harappan seals?
questions.explanation:
Unicorn is correct: a one-horned animal, called the unicorn, is the most common motif on Harappan seals.
Lion, Peacock and Camel are incorrect: none of these is the common seal motif.
So the answer is Unicorn.
